contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok; 404 on create_alias of a missing collection; 404/500 on delete_alias of an unknown alias
contract_grounding.note: Dispatch constraint_id field was empty; the anchor was recovered verbatim from the attack string and the script header (# constraint_ids: qdrant_behavioral_aliases_update_001) and exists in structured_contract.json. violates=true grounding: the observed element {"create_alias":{...complete...},"delete_alias":{...complete...}} is outside the declared per-element domain array[create_alias|delete_alias|rename_alias] under the exclusive one-of reading (all three doc examples carry exactly one discriminator per element; the gRPC proto oneof structurally enforces one; the endpoint's published '4XX: error' response family covers invalid requests), and the server executed only the create while silently discarding the requested delete and reporting result:true (sibling-script state evidence). Honest counterpoints for the auditor: (1) the behavioral assertion's own status matrix does not by itself mandate a 4xx for malformed shape — the violation grounds in the registry's declared actions element type plus the documented 4XX error family; (2) the published OpenAPI schema for AliasOperations is anyOf with NO additionalProperties:false, under whose strict letter a dual-key element validates against the CreateAliasOperation branch — the auditor must weigh the exclusive reading against the permissive schema letter.
